title: Episode 4 of Power, Planning, and Politics is on Bsquiklehausen's channel
premise: Donoteat redirects viewers to a collaboration, jokes about beer and political recruitment, previews future topics, and prolongs a goodbye while telling everyone to leave for the actual episode.
coverage: A static DNE token alternates with five beer containers, an Amtrak locomotive, housing and an armored bulldozer. Brief transitions may be missed; cut times are approximate.

panels.heading: The missing episode is elsewhere
panels.description: A round DNE transit-fare token sits at the center of a black screen as the narrator directs viewers to the collaborator’s channel.
panels.camera: Static centered token after a black opening.
panels.action: The narrator directs viewers to the other video; no presenter appears on screen.
panels.visualGag: The impersonal fare token stands in for the narrator, with GOOD FOR ONE FARE around DNE.

panels.heading: Five beers, counted on screen
panels.description: Two Neshaminy Creek The Shape of Hops to Come cans appear left of the token, and three Flying Fish Red Fish bottles appear to the right: exactly five beer containers.
panels.camera: Beer-container images flank the centered token.
panels.action: Five beer containers illustrate the narrator’s drinking disclaimer.
panels.visualGag: The picture counts out the narrator’s five beers.

panels.heading: Accessible history as political recruitment
panels.description: The beer containers disappear; the token returns alone against black while the narrator undercuts his claim that the collaboration is not terribly political.
panels.action: The token stays fixed as the narrator promises more overt politics in the forthcoming Organized Labor episode.

panels.heading: Railway critique gets a locomotive insert
panels.description: A photograph of an Amtrak locomotive replaces the token at the railway-topic announcement.
panels.camera: Cut to a static locomotive photograph, then back to the token.
panels.action: The locomotive photograph replaces the emblem.
panels.visualGag: The locomotive photograph abruptly punctuates the narrator’s dry list of future topics.

panels.heading: Option one: Red Vienna
panels.description: A photograph of a red-and-cream housing complex replaces the token during the Red Vienna option.
panels.camera: Cut to a static wide architectural photograph.
panels.action: The housing photograph holds as the narrator offers a Patreon-bonus topic choice.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the visual contrast between a housing-development topic and the armored-bulldozer topic in the next panel.
panels.notes: The building’s exact identity is uncertain.

panels.heading: Option two wins: Killdozer
panels.description: A photograph of an armored bulldozer with a yellow blade and damaged buildings replaces the housing photograph.
panels.camera: Cut to a static bulldozer photograph.
panels.action: The bulldozer is motionless in the photograph. The narrator declares his preference for this topic.
panels.visualGag: The sharp visual jump from civic housing to an armored bulldozer pays off the incongruous choice; the stated preference doubles down on it.

panels.heading: The goodbye that keeps adding things
panels.description: The centered token returns while the narrator asks viewers to watch the linked episode, then adds Patreon and social-media promotion.
panels.camera: Static centered token through the prolonged goodbye.
panels.action: The token stays fixed while the narrator keeps talking and tells the audience to leave for the other video.
panels.visualGag: The emblem remains unchanged through a self-defeating goodbye: the narrator keeps adding things while asking everyone to leave.

panels.heading: Closing tail
panels.description: The token remains on black after the farewell.
panels.notes: The collaboration is Historic Urbanism 101 on Bsquiklehausen’s channel.
